## The Core Claim

Real human and organizational decision-makers do not, and computationally cannot, optimize over the full space of possible alternatives to find a global-maximum choice; they 'satisfice' -- search a limited space using heuristics until an option meeting an acceptable threshold is found, then stop. This same bounded-search structure -- heuristic pruning of an intractably large search space to reach a good-enough solution within real time and memory limits -- is the literal design principle behind heuristic search algorithms in artificial intelligence, a link Simon made explicit while co-founding that field with Newell. Herbert Simon won the 1978 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for this theory of decision-making within economic organizations.
